title: MBIE Transition Fund: Supporting Continuity and Bold Innovation - World Today News
text:
The New Zealand Government is implementing a new funding strategy for the nation’s science, innovation, and technology system, centered on a new mechanism designed to provide research continuity and support high-impact developments.
A key element of this restructuring is the introduction of a Transition Research Fund, which has been announced for 2027. The fund is intended to provide stability for the research sector while simultaneously backing “bold ideas” and ensuring that science funding is closely aligned with national priorities.
The new strategy seeks to establish a simpler and more strategic framework for the science system. According to the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), the objective is to better assist researchers in turning scientific ideas into practical solutions that provide direct benefits to New Zealand.
This shift in funding represents a broader effort by the government to change how science, innovation, and technology are supported. By refocusing the system, the government aims to ensure that research investments are more effectively directed toward the country’s strategic needs.
MBIE, which is responsible for developing and supporting high-performing science and innovation to help shape the economy, is leading the implementation of this new approach. The ministry’s role includes delivering the policy and regulation necessary to support business growth and scientific advancement.
The rollout of the Transition Research Fund is scheduled to proceed in 2027.
